hidden_mutation_check.expected_repair_class: command content: remove the duplicate unlock while preserving the remaining sequence

reasons: Cause match: the hidden mutation is 'insert one duplicate `unlock north_gate with credential/gaoler_key` immediately after the original successful unlock', expected cause 'the second command repeats unlock after north_gate.access already transitioned from locked to closed'. The subject diagnosis (artifacts/diagnosis.md sec.1-2) names exactly that: lines 2 and 3 of failing.commands are byte-identical, the first unlock committed locked->closed, and the second was evaluated against `closed` where north_gate.access defines no `unlock` transition. This is the actual semantic cause, not a symptom restatement.

Distinguishing evidence cited and independently confirmed: EK0804 '`north_gate.access.unlock` is illegal while the machine is `closed`' with exit 1 and empty stderr (forensics/failure.stdout.json, failure.exit.txt); committed_command_count 1; state-hashes rows fa7247d1...50fe42 (ordinal 0) and b8eac772...94952b (ordinal 1); single command-log row; causal receipt tick 1 transition {from: locked, to: closed, namespace: north_gate.access, phase: local, cause command unlock}. Every one of these values was re-read by me from /workspace/input/debug-evidence and matches the diagnosis verbatim.

Independent reproduction of the failure: `bin/nomos run input/debug-evidence/world/ --commands input/debug-evidence/failing.commands` exited 1 with result_digest 0989bf6abcafe8c3e7c00a824a54a6c4b5f5ebafcb856215584748ba5713e988, EK0804, committed_command_count 1; all six emitted bundle members are cmp-identical to input/debug-evidence/failing.run/*, and also cmp-identical to the subject's artifacts/repro.run/*.

All six members are cmp-identical to the subject's artifacts/repaired.run/*.

Repair targets the owning boundary and matches the expected repair class: `diff failing.commands repaired.commands` yields exactly `3d2` with the single deleted line `unlock north_gate with credential/gaoler_key` (194 -> 149 bytes), i.e. command-script content only; the sealed world package, the binary, and the remaining command order were left untouched. Each observed code equals the code the subject reported, and all four subject probe bundles are cmp-identical to my regenerated ones, so alternatives A1-A2 are genuinely discriminated rather than asserted. World/compiler defect (A4), runtime/evidence defect (A5), schema/state-version mismatch (A6) and non-determinism/stale input (A7) are excluded consistently with the byte-identical reproduction and the intact hash chain.
